s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of skin and muscle symptoms following immunotherapy
salient_findings: Prominent erythema at nailfolds with dilated capillary loops
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Stage IV B-RAF V600E mutant malignant melanoma with metastases
Developed skin symptoms within 2 weeks of starting ipilimumab treatment
Received a second course of ipilimumab 14 months later
Physical findings include photodistributed erythematous to violaceous eruption
Diffuse erythema of forehead and midface
Erythema and edema of upper eyelids
Creatine kinase level increased to 1854 U/L
Aldolase level was 23.0 U/L
C-reactive protein level was 28.6 mg/L
Antinuclear antibody titer was 1:640 with speckled pattern
Jo-1 antibody was negative
MRI showed mild short TI inversion recovery hyperintensity of bilateral vastus lateralis and rectus femoris muscles
Vastus lateralis muscle biopsy showed atrophy of type II muscle fibers

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of skin and muscle symptoms, elevated creatine kinase level, and characteristic skin findings

shortlist.label: Ipilimumab-induced dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Temporal association with ipilimumab treatment and characteristic skin findings

shortlist.label: Polymyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated creatine kinase level and muscle weakness

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Association with underlying malignancy (melanoma) and characteristic skin findings

shortlist.label: Autoimmune myopathy associated with malignancy
shortlist.why_kept: Association with underlying malignancy (melanoma) and elevated creatine kinase level

raw.rationale: The patient developed skin symptoms within 2 weeks of starting ipilimumab treatment, and the symptoms recurred and worsened after a second course of ipilimumab, suggesting a strong temporal relationship between ipilimumab therapy and the development of dermatomyositis-like symptoms.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms are consistent with dermatomyositis, the temporal relationship with ipilimumab therapy suggests a drug-induced cause.

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and biopsy results are more consistent with dermatomyositis than polymyositis, which typically lacks skin involvement.

rejected.label: Paraneoplastic dermatomyositis
rejected.why: While the patient has a malignancy, the temporal relationship between ipilimumab therapy and symptom development suggests a drug-induced cause rather than a paraneoplastic phenomenon.

rejected.label: Autoimmune myopathy associated with malignancy
rejected.why: This diagnosis is too broad and does not specifically account for the patient's dermatomyositis-like symptoms and the temporal relationship with ipilimumab therapy.
